items.title: Novo notches up to $1.4B pact with Orbis to develop oral macrocycle cardiometabolic drugs
items.snippet: The multi-drug partnership with Orbis Medicines—which Novo has backed since the biotech's seed rounds—is focused on cardiometabolic targets, but the technology at the center of the deal could deliver oral weight loss candidates. Obesity rival Eli Lilly has also helped fund Orbis.

items.title: Webinar: Manufacturing in Turbulent Times
items.snippet: Learn what manufacturing challenges lie ahead, how to equip your team to protect your program from avoidable manufacturing and regulatory setbacks and forge partnerships that can withstand the next five years of industry turbulence.

items.title: Fed rate hike won’t hold biotech down despite climbing capital costs
items.snippet: While increases in the interest rate from the Federal Reserve are usually bad for biotech, the sector at this moment is poised to withstand the blow, according to analysts, though earlier stage companies may be left in the lurch.

items.title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
items.snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

items.title: Novartis drops $125M for Sironax’s tech to cross blood-brain barrier
items.snippet: Novartis stands alongside Big Pharma peers that have similarly invested in technologies to penetrate the blood-brain barrier, including GSK, Roche and Eli Lilly.

items.title: Longeveron’s shares crash as stem cell therapy flunks mid-stage cardio trial
items.snippet: With just over $10 million in cash available to fuel operations through the end of the year, Longeveron is undertaking a strategic review after the failure of a cardiovascular study.

items.title: Roche bets up to $1B to advance next-gen bispecifics with Dualitas
items.snippet: The partners will focus R&D efforts on immunological and inflammatory conditions using Dualitas’ DualScreen Bispecific Discovery Engine platform.

items.title: When vision fades: Rethinking wet AMD and the durability gap
items.snippet: In this episode of Denatured, you’ll hear Philip Jacob Rosenfeld, professor of Ophthalmology at the University of Miami Health System and Bascom Palmer Eye Institute, and Wesley Jackson, chief science officer at Valitor. We talk about the eye condition call wet age-related macular degeneration (AMD), the limits of ant...

items.title: Biopharma hiring hotspots: States, disciplines where demand is highest
items.snippet: As biopharma job openings rose this year, opportunities were greatest in Massachusetts and California and in the science/R&D and clinical disciplines, according to BioSpace data. Several other locations and functions have also been going strong.

items.title: Trending: Top biopharma disciplines with jobs live now
items.snippet: From engineering to science/R&D, these top seven biopharma disciplines each have hundreds, and in one case over 1,000, positions posted on BioSpace.

items.title: Sionna says good-bye to 46% of staffers, including exec
items.snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

items.title: FDA warning letter accuses Bausch & Lomb of lacking commitment to remediation
items.snippet: After reviewing Bausch & Lomb’s response to its observations, the FDA questioned whether the company is committed to implementing significant design remediations.

items.title: Deep dive: Psychedelics back on FDA’s doorstep
items.snippet: BioSpace takes stock of the psychedelic therapeutics space, which is once again on the cusp of its first FDA approval.

items.title: Novartis halts TREM2 targeting ALS program in 4th trial stumble in a month
items.snippet: The TREM2 stabilizer failed to show efficacy in a Phase 2 trial of patients with early-stage ALS. This development follows two late-stage trial failures reported by Novartis last week, plus the news that the pharma has paused multiple CAR T cell trials following patient deaths.

items.title: Sling catches $123M series C for thyroid eye disease pill
items.snippet: Sling Therapeutics is advancing the first late-stage oral drug for thyroid eye disease that, if approved, could compete against Amgen and Viridian Therapeutics.

items.title: 2026 IPO stock tracker: How newly public biotechs are performing
items.snippet: BioSpace is launching an IPO dashboard to help the industry keep tabs on U.S. biotechs that have taken the public plunge in 2026.

items.title: FDA hears input on psychedelics, PDUFA, lung cancer’s next-gen therapies boost survival
items.snippet: The FDA held a public forum on Monday to discuss the future of psychedelic therapeutics, followed by a meeting on Wednesday regarding recommendations for reauthorizing the Prescription Drug User Fee Act the day after launching its TrialBlazer initiative. Meanwhile, Definium Therapeutics notched another late-stage tria...

items.title: AI is changing the talent biotech companies compete to hire
items.snippet: As AI becomes more embedded in biotech R&D, companies are competing for professionals who can bridge biology, machine learning, data and engineering. Recruiting expert Darren Nelson explains which capabilities are becoming hardest to find—and why.

items.title: For many, the retirement goal posts are shifting
items.snippet: Biopharma professionals are among those delaying retirement, with 52% expecting to leave the workforce later than originally planned, according to a BioSpace LinkedIn poll. A career coach and recruiter discuss why some are pushing out or moving up their exits.

items.title: 5 biotechs braving the commercial waters with product launches
items.snippet: A growing number of biotechs are entering the market with newly launched medicines, a pattern indicative of “improving capital markets,” according to Jefferies’ Andrew Tsai.

items.title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
items.snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
items.snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.

items.title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?
items.snippet: Congressional letters sent to the CEOs of Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, BMS and AbbVie this week voicing concerns about the pharmas' clinical trials in China highlight an ongoing discrepancy in how government and industry think about the rise of the Asian country’s biotech industry.
